html:
The Namazga culture is a sequence of farming towns in the foothills of the Kopet Dag mountains in southern Turkmenistan, named after the large mound of Namazga-Tepe east of Ashgabat. Its six phases run from the fourth millennium BCE into the second.

It grew out of the earlier Jeitun culture, the first farmers of Central Asia. The Namazga people watered wheat and barley fields from mountain streams, made fine painted pottery and worked copper. In the Bronze Age, around 2500 to 2000 BCE, the largest sites such as Altyn-Depe became small towns with temples, craft quarters and walls, and had contacts as far as Iran and the Indus.

Around 2000 BCE the towns shrank and life moved east into the Murghab delta, where the Oxus Civilisation flourished.
